key_insight: TiRex-2 extends the TiRex time-series foundation model from univariate to multivariate forecasting, while also supporting streaming data and known future covariates. It aims to capture joint variable dynamics more efficiently than Transformer-based approaches.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of forecasting real-world time series where multiple variables evolve together, observations arrive sequentially over time, and some covariates are only known in the future. Existing Transformer-based foundation models can model cross-variable relationships, but they are costly in long contexts and often rely on full-history processing.
method: Uses an xLSTM-based recurrent architecture to model multivariate time series in a sequential, streaming-friendly way.
Generalizes the original TiRex framework to incorporate both past covariates and future-known covariates for forecasting.
Targets efficient long-context forecasting by avoiding the quadratic complexity typical of Transformer-based models.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it offers a more scalable way to do multivariate forecasting in real operational settings, such as finance, energy, and sensor systems. It combines stronger temporal modeling with lower inference complexity for continuous data streams.

paper_title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming
